title: Elastic panel reflow and canvas fallback strategy for metrics & rollout pages
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Several console surfaces (cost dashboards, rollout detail pages, and the experiments charting canvas) have brittle reflow behavior at narrow viewports and on non-Chrome browsers. Issues reported by platform and customer-facing teams include clipped axis labels on Firefox, modal overflow on iPad landscape, and janky chart redraws when panels are resized. Goal: implement a unified layout strategy that keeps tables and charts readable across breakpoints, provides a deterministic modal stacking model, and introduces a canvas fallback path for browsers with GPU/text-rendering anomalies. This ticket captures design proposals, acceptance criteria, prototype links, and cross-team handoff notes. Scope: UX patterns for: 1) dashboard metric cards and multi-panel reflow; 2) horizontal tables with responsive column collapsing; 3) chart canvas fallback (SVG/HTML layer) and axis label trimming; 4) modal and rollout drawer stacking rules; 5) keyboard + screen-reader considerations for collapsed content. Out of scope: backend telemetry changes and new analytics data collection (separate ENG task).
acceptance_criteria: Metric and chart panels reflow without overlap at 320px, 375px, 768px, and 1024px breakpoints
Tables with >6 columns collapse into a priority-driven summary row with an expandable detail tray on mobile
Charts fall back to an SVG/text-rendered layer on browsers where canvas axis rendering is inconsistent (notably Firefox on macOS and Safari iOS) and preserve accessibility labels
Modals/drawers honor a single stacking context: drawers take precedence on the right, modals center; z-index rules documented and implemented
No visual regressions on desktop Chrome; visual diffs for Firefox/Safari validated by QA and design
Keyboard navigation and focus traps work for collapsed table detail trays and rollout modals, with aria-expanded/aria-controls implemented
Performance budget: initial panel paint and first-interactive remain within current SLO (no more than 15% regression in synthetic lighthouse median for affected pages)
design_proposals: Adaptive grid: switch from a 12-column fixed to a fluid fractional grid for metric cards; on <560px switch to stacked single-column with condensed badges

Table priority collapse: annotate columns with a visual-priority token (critical, useful, optional). Critical columns remain visible; optional columns collapse into an inline 'More' action that toggles a stacked detail tray

Chart rendering: default runtime is GPU-accelerated canvas. When feature-detecting a canvas text-measurement mismatch (text widths differ across reflows or rendering artifacts appear), swap to an SVG layer that mirrors canvas geometry for axes and labels. Keep the same paint ordering using a shared data pipeline from the chart renderer (runtime hook implemented by ENG).

Modal & drawer rules: 1) drawers slide from right, full-height; 2) modals center with 88% max-width on desktop, 96% on tablet; 3) when both are open, drawer receives inert attribute to avoid dual focus traps; 4) ESC closes top-most layer; 5) backdrop opacity reduced on mobile to keep content legible behind overlays
Accessibility: collapsed trays include a visible affordance and screen reader hint (e.g., 'Show 3 more columns for this row'). Use role=region and aria-labelledby for chart summaries.
decisions: Use feature-detection instead of user-agent sniffing for canvas fallbacks
Prefer progressive disclosure (collapsed trays) over horizontal scrolling for table overflow on touch devices
Keep current color/spacing tokens; avoid introducing new tokens for this iteration to reduce engineering churn
Defer iconography updates to a follow-up ticket; use existing chevrons and ellipsis actions
tasks: Finalize Figma frames for 4 breakpoints and annotate constraints
Pair with ENG to implement canvas->SVG fallback hook and add a small compatibility test harness
Document z-index stacking rules and update global theme layer in the console CSS variables
Design QA pass: create visual-diff baseline images for Chrome, Firefox, and Safari at each breakpoint
Create keyboard/voiceover test checklist and run with Accessibility team
Ship a canary release behind a feature flag and monitor for layout regressions via the console telemetry dashboard
